f.title: Classify an event as life-threatening only if it placed the subject at immediate risk of death

It does not include an event or reaction that might have caused death had it occurred in a more severe form.

f.title: Consider important medical events serious when they may jeopardise the subject and need intervention
f.statement: Important medical events that may not result in death, be life-threatening, or require hospitalization may be considered serious when, based upon appropriate medical judgment, they may jeopardize the patient or subject and may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the serious outcomes. (The definition goes on to give examples: allergic bronchospasm treated in an emergency room or at home, blood dyscrasias or convulsions without hospitalization, drug dependency or abuse; these are outside the quote.)

f.title: Treat an adverse event as a suspected adverse reaction when there is evidence suggesting a causal relationship
f.statement: A suspected adverse reaction is any adverse event for which there is a reasonable possibility that the drug caused it. For IND safety reporting, "reasonable possibility" means there is evidence to suggest a causal relationship between the drug and the adverse event. A suspected adverse reaction implies a lesser degree of certainty about causality than an adverse reaction, which is any adverse event caused by a drug.

f.title: A safety report is not an admission of causality; the sponsor need not admit and may deny it
f.statement: A safety report or other information submitted by a sponsor under part 312 (and any release of it by FDA) does not necessarily reflect a conclusion by the sponsor or FDA that it constitutes an admission that the drug caused or contributed to an adverse event. A sponsor need not admit, and may deny, that the report or information it submitted constitutes such an admission.
